exceptions.title: stays focusable through inputRef
exceptions.reason: The case gives the React ref prop `inputRef`. A part of Vase UI exposes its input as `inputElement`, and a part cannot know if a consumer reads an exposed member. With no `name`, no `autoComplete`, no `required` and no field, the input thus stays `type="hidden"`, which cannot take the focus. A consumer that focuses the input gives the control one of them.

exceptions.title: updates merged refs and event handlers when ref shape changes across rerenders
exceptions.reason: A part gives its ref callbacks one time, in `setup`, so their shape cannot change. React makes a new merged ref when the `ref` argument changes. A new test covers the handler half: a listener of the part that changes between two renders.

exceptions.title: syncs replacement refs without publishing an unchanged map
exceptions.reason: The case replaces the ref objects of a mounted list. A Vue part gives `elementsRef` and `labelsRef` one time, in `setup`. The new case `does not publish an unchanged map when a label changes` covers the half that applies.
React hides a mounted tree and detaches its refs when a component in it suspends again. A mounted Vue component cannot suspend again.

exceptions.title: uses a render element's own label instead of the trigger
exceptions.reason: The case gives a React element with an `aria-label` as `render`. In Vue `#render` is a slot, which is a function, so the part does not see an attribute of the element of the slot. `resolvePopupLabel` reads the attributes of the part.

The file reads the id of a React element that is given as `render`. It gives the id to the owner through a ref callback. In Vue, `#render` is a slot, so a part reads the `id` of the element only after the render. `MenuPopup.vue` binds its `id` prop or the default id of the popup, and the store follows the `id` of the popup element (`VUE-73`). The filter root reads the `id` of the list element with `useElementId`. A part that another part names reads the `id` of its own element from the mount on, with `useRegisteredId`.

Vase UI has no such function. The block `prop: id` of this test covers the `id` of the popup element that the trigger names, the default id after a removal, an `id` and an empty `id` from the `#render` slot, and the release at unmount. `packages/vue/src/filter-dropdown/list/FilterDropdownList.test.tsx` covers the release for the list and the id that the `#render` slot gives the list (`VUE-117`). `packages/vue/src/menu/filter-root/MenuFilterRoot.test.tsx` covers an empty `id` prop, which counts as no id (`VUE-93`), and an empty id from the `#render` slot. The cases that read the props of a `render` element are for React.
The file adds the matcher `toEqualDateTime`. Only the shared suite of the temporal adapters calls it, and Vase UI does not port that suite.
The helper flushes React before and after a move of the fake clock. A ported test calls `flushMicrotasks` and `vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync`, which run the flushes of Vue.
The helper merges React ref objects and ref callbacks. A Vue element takes one `ref`, so a test component gives it one function that calls each setter.
`packages/vue/test/setup.ts` moves the real pointer of the browser off the page after each test that put it there. A test file thus needs no call.
`isScrollLocked` of `packages/vue/test/fixtures/scrollDocument.ts` does this work. It reads the computed overflow of the element that scrolls the page, and the marker `data-vase-ui-scroll-locked`.
The file declares the type of a CSS module. No Vase UI test imports a CSS module. A test component sets its styles as style objects.
